answer: Macrophages contribute to prenatal skin blood vessel formation: they co-locate with endothelial cells in neurovascular microenvironments, express pro-angiogenic gene programs, and interactions between macrophages and endothelial cells are required to support angiogenesis and blood vessel remodelling (e.g., macrophage-expressed VEGFA regulates GATA2 activity in endothelial cells, and adding macrophages to skin organoids produced a more elaborate, organized vascular network).
support_quote: Collectively, our findings demonstrate that interactions between macrophages and endothelial cells are required to support angiogenesis through blood vessel remodelling.
